'''''Tripleurospermum maritimum''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Asteraceae|aster family]] commonly known as '''false mayweed''' or '''sea mayweed'''. It is found in many coastal areas of [[Northern Europe]], including [[Scandinavia]] and [[Iceland]], often growing in sand or amongst beach pebbles.

==Description==
''Tripleurospermum maritimum'' is a [[herbaceous]] plant that grows as a [[biennial plant|biennial]] or short-lived [[perennial plant|perennial]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Clapham |first1=A. R. |author1-link=Arthur Roy Clapham |title=Excursion Flora of the British Isles |date=1981 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge; New York |isbn=978-0-521-23290-6 |page=333 |url=https://archive.org/details/excursionfloraof0000clap_t0h8 |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref> They are usually [[procumbent]], grow along the ground before turning upwards towards the end, but may grow straight upwards. Most often they reach {{convert|10 to 80|cm|0|sp=us}} in length.<ref name="Fedorov">{{Cite book |last1=Fedorov |first1=Andrey A. |author-link1=Andrey A. Fedorov |date=1976 |chapter=''Campanula'' |editor-last1=Tutin |editor-first1=T.G. |editor-link1=Tom Tutin |editor-last2=Heywood |editor-first2=V.H. |editor-link2=Vernon Heywood |editor-last3=Burges |editor-first3=N.A. |editor-link3=Alan Burges |editor-last4=Moore |editor-first4=D.M. |editor-link4=David Moore (botanist born 1933) |editor-last5=Valentine |editor-first5=D.H. |editor-link5=David H. Valentine |editor-last6=Walters |editor-first6=S.M. |editor-link6=Max Walters |editor-last7=Webb |editor-first7=D.A. |editor-link7=D. A. Webb |title=Flora Europaea |url=https://archive.org/details/floraeuropaea0004tuti |url-access=registration |language=en |volume=4 Plantaginaceae to Compositae (and Rubiaceae) |location=Cambridge, England |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=166 |isbn=978-0-521-08717-9 |oclc=751554359 |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref> The leaves are divided with the ending segments narrow with a fleshy, succulent texture.<ref name="Rune">{{Cite book |last1=Rune |first1=Flemming |date=2011 |title=Wild Flowers of Greenland = Grønlands Vilde Planter |url=https://archive.org/details/wildflowersofgre0000rune |url-access=registration |language=en, da |edition=first |location=Hillerød, Denmark; Qeqertarsuaq, Greenland |publisher=Gyldenlund Publishing, in collaboration with Arctic Station, University of Copenhagen |page=294 |isbn=978-87-993172-5-7 |oclc=794007591 |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref>

The daisy-like [[flowering heads]] measure from {{cvt|3 to 5.5|cm}} across.<ref name="Rune" /> The seeds are [[achene]]s that measure 1.8 to 3.5 mm long and can be pale to blackish-brown.<ref name="Fedorov" />

==Taxonomy==
''Tripleurospermum maritimum'' was given the scientific name ''Matricaria maritima'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. The botanist [[Wilhelm Daniel Joseph Koch]] moved it to the genus ''[[Tripleurospermum]]'' in 1845 giving the species its accepted name. With the rest of its genus it is part of the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref name="POWO" />

==Range and habitat==
According to [[Plants of the World Online]] it is native to Europe, Greenland, and the Azores. It grows in all of the [[Scandinavian countries]] and the [[British Isles]]. South of the [[Baltic Sea]] it is native to the [[Baltic States]], Northwest European Russia near St. Petersburg, Poland, and Germany. In the west it is also native to France, Spain, and Portugal.<ref name="POWO" />

It usually grows near the ocean in open habitats.<ref name="Fedorov" /> On the seashore it grows upper parts of the habitat. It also grows in disused and human disturbed areas.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hackney |first1=Paul |title=Stewart & Corry's Flora of the North-east of Ireland : Vascular Plant and Charophyte Sections |date=1992 |publisher=Institute of Irish Studies, Queen's University of Belfast |location=Belfast, Northern Ireland |isbn=978-0-85389-446-9 |page=294 |url=https://archive.org/details/stewartcorrysflo0000hack |url-access=registration |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref>
